To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ultra-low clay content localized along micrometer thick layers in calcite-rich gouges facilitates seismic slip propagation during earthquake ruptures in continental domains.
ultra-thin clay layers (<1 µm thick) facilitate seismic slip in carbonates.
ultra-thin phyllosilicte-bearing layers can facilitate seismic rupture in calcite-hosted faults.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of ultra-thin clay layers in the seismic slip of carbonate-hosted seimogenic faults.
the identification of phyllosilicic lubrication mechanisms that facilitate seismic slip in carbonates, which can be used to improve seismic hazard assessment in continental domains.
the role of phyllosilicatic-bearing micro-layers in facilitating seismic slip along carbonate faults, with important implications for seismic hazard assessment in continental domains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
phyllosi-licates facilitate seismic slip propagation along carbonate faults, but the amount of phyllosi- licate required to facilitate slip is not yet known.
phyllosili-cates can facilitate seismic slip along oceanic subducting faults, but not necessarily in continental domains.

phyllosite layers are a key factor for earthquake nucleation and propagation in continental domains, but not in oceanic domains, because of the different clay content and thicknesses of the phyllosilite layers in these two settings.

ultra-thin phyllosilicte-bearing layers can act as a lubricant for seismic slip propagation along faults in carbonate rocks.
